canonical_name: L1 adaptive control basic simulation (Hovakimyan & Cao's L1 architecture on a first-order plant with unknown parameters), MATLAB, run under Octave
lineage: L1 adaptive control (Cao & Hovakimyan, 2006-; book 2010): a state predictor, a fast projection-based adaptation law, and a low-pass filter on the control channel that decouples adaptation rate from robustness -- the adaptive architecture flown on NASA's AirSTAR and in quadrotor augmentation. This is a minimal simulation of the architecture (MATLAB, 2022) whose author later published L1 augmentation for geometric quadrotor control.
version: github.com/xkhainguyen/L1AC-Basics main (commit in hashes): MainL1_ODE1_v1.m, MainL1_ODE1_v2.m

source_identity.theory: Hovakimyan & Cao, L1 Adaptive Control Theory, SIAM 2010

compiler_or_interpreter: GNU Octave 7.3 (docker prometheus-fossil-octave:bookworm); plot calls shadowed

example.command: octave --no-gui -p $HARNESS MainL1_ODE1_v1.m; print the final tracking error and adapted parameter
example.output: the adapted estimate and the tracking error trace

upstream_docs: Hovakimyan & Cao, L1 Adaptive Control Theory: Guaranteed Robustness with Fast Adaptation, SIAM 2010

human_capability_summary.built_to: adapt fast to an unknown plant without the high-gain fragility of classical MRAC, by filtering the adaptive control signal
human_capability_summary.pressure: unknown/time-varying plant with robustness requirements (flight control)
human_capability_summary.success_means: the plant tracks the reference; the adaptive estimate moves; the filtered control stays smooth

human_environmental_pressure: parametric uncertainty under a hard robustness margin
human_failure_condition: loss of robustness under fast adaptation (the MRAC failure L1 was designed against; Rohrs 1985)
behavioral_entry_point: the adaptation gain Gamma and the filter bandwidth in the script
